:::{#exr-ols-slope-r}
#### OLS slope and the correlation

Assuming $\sspred > 0$ and $\ssout > 0$ (@def-centered-sums),
write the OLS slope $\hcoef{x}$ from @thm-ols-slr
in terms of the
[Pearson correlation coefficient](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-pearson-r) $r$
and the
[sample standard deviations](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-sd)
$s_x$ and $s_y$ of the $\predvar_\iobs$ and the $\outvar_\iobs$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-ols-slope-r}

In terms of the centered sums (@def-centered-sums, @def-centered-cross-product),

$$
r = \frac{\sspredout}{\sqrt{\sspred \ssout}},
\qquad
s_x = \sqrt{\frac{\sspred}{n-1}},
\qquad
s_y = \sqrt{\frac{\ssout}{n-1}}.
$$

So:

$$
\begin{aligned}
r \, \frac{s_y}{s_x}
&= \frac{\sspredout}{\sqrt{\sspred \ssout}} \cdot
  \frac{\sqrt{\ssout / (n-1)}}{\sqrt{\sspred / (n-1)}}
&& \text{(substitute $r$, $s_x$, $s_y$)}\\
&= \frac{\sspredout}{\sqrt{\sspred} \sqrt{\ssout}} \cdot
  \frac{\sqrt{\ssout / (n-1)}}{\sqrt{\sspred / (n-1)}}
&& \text{(square root of a product)}\\
&= \frac{\sspredout}{\sqrt{\sspred} \sqrt{\ssout}} \cdot
  \frac{\sqrt{\ssout} / \sqrt{n-1}}{\sqrt{\sspred} / \sqrt{n-1}}
&& \text{(square root of a quotient)}\\
&= \frac{\sspredout}{\sqrt{\sspred} \sqrt{\ssout}} \cdot
  \frac{\sqrt{\ssout}}{\sqrt{\sspred}}
&& \text{(cancel the factors of $\sqrt{n - 1}$)}\\
&= \frac{\sspredout \sqrt{\ssout}}{\sqrt{\sspred} \sqrt{\ssout} \sqrt{\sspred}}
&& \text{(multiply the fractions)}\\
&= \frac{\sspredout}{\sqrt{\sspred} \sqrt{\sspred}}
&& \text{(cancel $\sqrt{\ssout}$, which is positive)}\\
&= \frac{\sspredout}{\sspred}
&& \text{($\sqrt{\sspred} \sqrt{\sspred} = \sspred$)}\\
&= \hcoef{x}
&& \text{(closed-form OLS slope)}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
